searchText: Summary of breakout #10: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1523#issuecomment-2863738615 Shorter summary of breakout #10: https://x.com/jih2nn/status/1920539090035892672 opened a PR in `ethereum/execution-specs` for focil. it currently contains a lot of the boilerplate for the new osaka fork, but that will only remain until there is a `forks/osaka` branch and then we will rebase. you can find the changes for focil in `src/ethereum/osaka/fork.py` and function name `validate_inclusion_list`, which is called inside `apply_body` optimistic attesting comes with complicated fork-choice modifications. Maybe this doesn't make much of a difference when thinking of ePBS x FOCIL since there's already a new modified fork-choice rule, but for delayed execution, it was not really considered because of fork choice complexities that come from potentially keeping invalid blocks in the store. I still think the bitlist solution, with the lists in the block, is way cleaner and simpler here. Ah yes, I am totally open to the idea that delayed execution will have other ways for integrating with FOCIL that are good. I was just coming from your recent ethresearch post that discusses optimistic attestations as one of the options, and wanted to offer a comparison to ePBS there. What are you referring to with the bitlist in the block? Forkchoice does not change at all In the sense that Forkchoice of ePBS + FOCIL = Forkchoice of ePBS Yeah, this was my sense! Gotcha Forkchoice of ePBS is not much changed from today though: it's minimal with the allowances for empty blocks let me look it up, it was a hackmd by francesco edit: sorry couldn't find it but in short: The proposer includes a bitlist indicating which IL committee members had their ILs considered. Also in block n, attesters verify that the appropriate transactions were "considered." This verification does not require execution; if all IL transactions were considered, the block is deemed "valid enough to attest to." Francesco had this but on the payload and the AC had that evaluation. What Anders' realized (or rather I with Ander's idea for something very similar) is that the builder can include these in the bid itself, so attesters, and not the AC can immediately vote Are we in the ePBS or delayed execution setting here? Perhaps you are referring to the mechanism where the AC votes on the bitfield? https://hackmd.io/UX7Vhsv8RTy8I49Uxez3Ng#Fork-choice The post on ABBs outlines the similarities and makes a small comparison. So delayed execution could in principle use the exact same mechanism of adding the bitlist to the block the problem with delayed execution is that the payload is committed so if the bitlist is not fullfiled the situation is much more dire than in ePBS and that's why its more complicated to make it work cleanly

excerpts.author: jacobkaufmann
excerpts.content:
opened a PR in `ethereum/execution-specs` for focil. it currently contains a lot of the boilerplate for the new osaka fork, but that will only remain until there is a `forks/osaka` branch and then we will rebase.

you can find the changes for focil in `src/ethereum/osaka/fork.py` and function name `validate_inclusion_list`, which is called inside `apply_body`

excerpts.author: nero_eth
excerpts.content:
optimistic attesting comes with complicated fork-choice modifications. Maybe this doesn't make much of a difference when thinking of ePBS x FOCIL since there's already a new modified fork-choice rule, but for delayed execution, it was not really considered because of fork choice complexities that come from potentially keeping invalid blocks in the store.
I still think the bitlist solution, with the lists in the block, is way cleaner and simpler here.

excerpts.author: nero_eth
excerpts.content:
let me look it up, it was a hackmd by francesco
edit: sorry couldn't find it but in short:
The proposer includes a bitlist indicating which IL committee members had their ILs considered. Also in block n, attesters verify that the appropriate transactions were "considered." This verification does not require execution; if all IL transactions were considered, the block is deemed "valid enough to attest to."

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Francesco had this but on the payload and the AC had that evaluation. What Anders' realized (or rather I with Ander's idea for something very similar) is that the builder can include these in the bid itself, so attesters, and not the AC can immediately vote
